newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expels two Indian envoys in retaliatory move. [CORRECTED 00:08 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. expels two Indian envoys in retaliatory move. [CORRECTED 00:08 GMT]

text.p: The United States has ordered the explusion of two diplomats from India in retaliation for the expulsion of one (corrects from two throughout the story) American official from New Dehli last month, a State Department spokesman said on Sunday.

Spokesman Glyn Davies said the Indian diplomats were stationed in the San Francisco and Chicago consulates and were ordered on Feb 10 to leave the country for "activities that were incompatible with their consular status."
The spokesman confirmed the decision to force out the diplomats was in retaliation for the expulsion of one American last month from New Delhi. No further details were available.

The American diplomat asked to leave India was reported to be the station chief of the CIA in New Dehli. The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the American reportedly had "unauthorized" links with a man called Rattan Sehgal, identified as a director in charge of the anti-espionage division of India's Intelligence Bureau.
"Following this Sehgal was asked to put in his papers which he did in late December...," the PTI said.
